title: Build image-compatibility graph & SBOM alignment for upgrade gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a canonical compatibility graph that links container image artifacts to their SBOM components, pinned CUDA/driver stacks, and validated kernel/OS compatibility. This graph will be the authoritative input to rollout gates, upgrade tooling, and the coordinator that decides safe model/image rollouts across Hosted/Dedicated/Private ships. The goal is to reduce upgrade incidents related to mismatched drivers or missing artifacts and to enable automated gating for LTS channel promotions.
background: We currently rely on ad-hoc mappings between image tags and driver pinsets maintained in spreadsheets and a few CI scripts. Incidents in Q4-2024 and early 2025 showed several rollouts failed because an image was built against a CUDA minor version not validated on the target driver bundle. There is also no single source of truth for SBOM-to-image relationships across registries. This ticket codifies that mapping and provides programmatic APIs for the rest of release tooling.
acceptance_criteria: A normalized compatibility graph stored in the artifact index service that exposes: image -> SBOM hash(s), image -> build CUDA version, image -> recommended pinned driver bundle key, kernel/os constraints (where applicable)
Automated reconciliation job that runs nightly to ingest new images from our registries and update graph edges; mismatches generate a triaged alert stream in the release-ops Slack channel
Rollout gate enrichment: the release coordinator can query the graph to block a rollout if target capacity lacks validated driver support (end-to-end test + graph check)
Documented schema and migration plan; no runtime callers are broken after rollout (backwards-compatible API versioning in place)
Integration tests that simulate a mismatched image-driver scenario and assert the gate blocks the canary rollout
tasks: Design compatibility graph schema (nodes: image, sbom, driver-bundle, host-profile; edges with properties)
Implement SBOM ingestion lambda to fetch/normalize SPDX/CycloneDX blobs and compute canonical hashes
Extend artifact-index service APIs to store and expose graph edges
Nightly reconciler: discover images, validate SBOM contents, infer CUDA/toolchain version, propose driver bundle mapping
Create release-coordinator check that queries graph and returns gating decisions with human-readable reasons
Add dashboards for mismatch rates and ingestion lag in Grafana
Write e2e test harness and add to canary pipeline
progress_updates: 2025-03-02: Kickoff with Release Infra, Runtime, and Security. Agreed on graph-first approach instead of ad-hoc rules (notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Image+Compat+Graph)
2025-03-05: Schema proposal v0.1 posted; favors simple typed edges to remain storage-efficient. Feedback from Runtime team: include 'kv_cache_behavior' flag per image (PRD link shared)
2025-03-08: PoC SBOM normalizer finished (branch: github.com/redwood/release-infra/tree/eng-26789-sbom-normalizer). Normalizer supports SPDX and CycloneDX and emits canonical sha256 identifier
2025-03-11: Integration discussion with Ops: nightly reconciler will run in us-west-2 and emit findings to release-ops channel. Ops requested rate limits and backoff to avoid registry throttling

2025-03-14: First end-to-end flow created in dev environment: image -> sbom ingestion -> inferred CUDA 11.8 -> matched to driver-bundle 'db-2025-03-11-cu118' (internal index). Test canary blocked when simulated missing driver-bundle
2025-03-18: Security review checklist started; security requested proof that SBOM ingestion does not execute any untrusted code. Added sandbox step and content-type validation
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: store canonical graph in artifact-index (Postgres) rather than a separate graph DB to reduce operational surface and keep join-friendly queries for release coordinator
Tradeoff: using heavyweight graph DB would simplify some queries but increase ops cost. We chose relational + adjacency table with indexes for performance
Decision: nightly reconciler vs event-driven ingestion. Nightly chosen initially to reduce registry quota consumption; we will revisit if lag is problematic
Tradeoff: pinning driver bundles strictly prevents flexibility for Dedicated hosts with custom drivers. To mitigate, graph will include 'flexible' badge for images validated against a driver range
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on schema extensibility (new node types) and API stability contract. Validate that the reconciler's inference heuristics (parsing ld.so versions, testing CUDA binary symbols) are documented and auditable.
qa_plan: Unit tests for SBOM normalizer, integration tests for reconciler + index, canary job that intentionally creates an image with mismatched driver to assert gating. Manual review of first 100 ingestion events.
post_rollout_tasks: Monitor mismatch dashboard for two weeks and tune heuristics
Add ability to auto-propose driver-bundle backfills for images missing recommended bundles
Run a dry-run LTS promotion using the graph to validate no blocking false-positives
